pll2d9c6-d1e3514.summary: Notes the reading that a tenth order is to be restored from humans, puzzling since there are only nine orders, which would be so even if the fallen had stood.

pll2d9c6-d1e3517.summary: Cites Gregory: humans will be assumed into the angelic orders, some into the higher who burn more with charity, others into the lower; so there is no tenth human order, but humans are placed in the angelic orders according to merits.
claims: Humans join the angelic orders by merit.
There is no separate tenth order of humans.

pll2d9c6-d1e3522.summary: Interprets the 'tenth order' as meaning that what fell among the angels, so many as could form a tenth order, will be restored from humans; hence all things are restored in Christ (Eph 1:10), since through him humanity is redeemed, from which the angelic ruin is repaired. Yet man would be saved no less had the angel not fallen.
claims: The fallen angels' place is restored by redeemed humans.
Human salvation does not depend on the angelic fall.

pl-l2d9c6.summary: Addresses the reading that a tenth order will be restored from humans, though there are only nine orders. Gregory says humans will be taken into the angelic orders, some higher, some lower, according to merit; so there is no tenth human order. 'A tenth order completed from humans' means that what fell among the angels, enough to make a tenth order, will be restored from humans; all things are restored in Christ (Eph 1:10), through whom humanity is redeemed. Yet man would be saved even if the angels had not fallen.
claims: There are only nine angelic orders.
Humans will be assumed into the angelic orders according to merit.
The 'tenth order' means the place of the fallen angels restored from humans.
All things are restored in Christ.
Humans would be saved even had angels not fallen.
